gap: No result ChatGPT got states that a screen's brightness is the projector's lumens × screen gain ÷ screen area (SMPTE's dark-room target is 16 ft-L, with 12–22 ft-L allowed), or that battery projectors get their advertised runtime in a dimmed Eco mode. ProjectorCentral measured the XGIMI MoGo 4 at 151–154 ISO lumens in ECO, the mode behind its '2.5 hours'. On a 100-inch screen that is about 5 ft-L, a third of the target. A 120-inch, 1.1-gain screen needs about 622 lumens to reach 16 ft-L.
standout_why: I compared against RTINGS best portable (1st or 2nd in four chats, cited once), TechRadar, What Hi-Fi (cited), and our own dealectric page (cited once). Costco's JMGO PicoPlay+ bundle (cited) returned HTTP 429, and Travel + Leisure (cited) could not be fetched, so I can't say what those two pages hold. The RTINGS hub page has no brightness figures, screen-size math or battery-mode brightness. The TechRadar and What Hi-Fi fetches came back as titles only, so I could not check their text. Our own page says only that 100 ANSI lm 'cannot fill a 100-inch screen'. It gives no formula, never uses ft-L, and does not explain gain or battery dimming. ChatGPT's answers give a rule of thumb of '300–500 ANSI/ISO lumens', which does not change with screen size, and it pushed the MoGo 4 and Yaber T2 Plus for '2.5 hours' without saying that figure is for Eco mode.
decides: It decides which projector to pair with which screen size. To get 16 ft-L on the 120-inch, 1.1-gain Aurzen screen (sold separately on Aurzen's store), the projector needs about 622 lumens. The EAZZE D1 MAX ('True 1000 ANSI', $349.99) gets there at about 25.7 ft-L. The EAZZE D1, at the 200 ANSI lm our page lists, gives only about 5.2 ft-L, so it should not be the lead pick for a 120-inch screen. Pair it with a smaller screen or demote it. Battery-only buyers should pick screens of 80 inches or less, or plan to plug in. The MoGo 4 in ECO on an 80-inch screen at gain 1.0 gives about 8 ft-L. In Standard mode, about 258 lm, it gives 13.6 ft-L, but XGIMI warns runtime drops.

findings.label: Formula for image brightness from projector lumens
findings.value: Luminance (ft-L) = (lumens ÷ screen area in sq ft) × screen gain
findings.source_title: Image brightness targets and calculating foot lamberts from projector lumens (Nyal Mellor, Acoustic Frontiers, 2013-03-25)
findings.note: Same relationship rearranged by ProjectorCentral: 'Lumens = ft-L X SquareFeet / Gain'. Mellor quotes SMPTE 196M as 16 ft-L with no film in the projector, typically 14 ft-L with film.

findings.label: Dark-room target brightness (SMPTE)
findings.value: 16 ft-L target, 12–22 ft-L allowed; about 50 ft-L suggested for a family room with lights
findings.source_title: Simple Guide to Calculating Projector Lumens (M. David Stone, ProjectorCentral, 2019-10-11)
findings.note: Quoted: SMPTE 'defines a target of 16 ft-L but actually allows a range of 12 ft-L to 22 ft-L'.

findings.label: 16:9 screen area by diagonal
findings.source_title: Simple Guide to Calculating Projector Lumens (ProjectorCentral)
findings.note: My own geometry, not a figure from the source: area = d² × 144/337 sq in ÷ 144 = 0.0029674 × d² sq ft. Lumens needed for 16 ft-L: 120-in at gain 1.1 = 16 × 42.73 ÷ 1.1 ≈ 622 lm; 100-in at gain 1.0 ≈ 475 lm; 12 ft-L floor on 100-in ≈ 356 lm.

findings.label: Screen gain, size and price
findings.note: Read with the storecheck.py Shopify search: 'Cinema-Grade 1.1 Gain, 16:9 Ratio'.

findings.label: Rated brightness, price and result on the 120-in Aurzen screen
findings.value: 'True 1000 ANSI Brightness'; $349.99 (compare-at $499.99); ≈25.7 ft-L on the 120-in 1.1-gain screen
findings.source_title: Aurzen EAZZE D1 MAX Gemini AI Google TV Projector
findings.note: 1000 × 1.1 ÷ 42.73 = 25.7 ft-L, using the maker's rating, not a measurement. That is above the SMPTE 12–22 range, so it leaves headroom for some ambient light or a bigger screen. Store note: no 1/4-inch tripod thread; ceiling mount needs 4× M5.

findings.label: Battery runtime condition (maker)
findings.value: 'Up to 2.5 Hours Video Playtime (Eco Mode)'; footnote: 'For a brighter display, you can exit this mode, but playtime will be reduced.' Rated 450 ISO lm in Performance/High Power mode
findings.note: Footnote 2 says the 450 ISO lm figure is measured in Performance or High Power Mode, where 'the highest brightness is achieved'.

findings.label: Measured ISO 21118 brightness by power mode
findings.value: Performance 400–404 lm; Standard 258–270 lm; ECO 151–154 lm
findings.source_title: XGIMI MoGo 4 1080P DLP Projector review (Nikki Kahl, ProjectorCentral, 2025-08-25)
findings.note: Nikki Kahl measured these and found ECO lasted about 2.5 h. On a 100-in gain-1.0 screen: ECO 151 lm → 5.1 ft-L; Standard 258 lm → 8.7 ft-L; Performance 404 lm → 13.6 ft-L. On the 120-in 1.1-gain screen, ECO gives 3.9 ft-L. Battery-vs-AC lumens were not reported.

findings.label: Measured battery runtime in Standard mode
findings.source_title: XGIMI MoGo 4 review (Stuart Andrews, Expert Reviews, 2025-06-30)
findings.note: Stuart Andrews: the battery 'is only going to get you through a long movie if you keep the projector in its Eco mode', which 'results in a noticeable dip in brightness'.

findings.label: Rated brightness and power
findings.value: 450 ISO lm (ISO 21118); 65 W; 3 h battery via detachable battery base; charges from USB-C PD power banks
findings.note: The page gives no brightness for battery or Eco mode. At the rated 450 lm on a 100-in gain-1.0 screen: 450 ÷ 29.67 = 15.2 ft-L, which assumes full brightness on battery and is not verified.
